DATED: 15/07/2024  undef  IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD  R/FIRST APPEAL NO. 5382 of 2019 ==========================================================
 THE UNITED INDIA INSURANCE CO LTD  Versus  BHARATBHAI GANESHBHAI BARAIYA & ORS.
==========================================================
Appearance:
MR RATHIN P RAVAL(5013) for the Appellant(s) No. 1 HCLS COMMITTEE(4998) for the Defendant(s) No. 3 MALAYKUMAR S PATEL(8901) for the Defendant(s) No. 1 MS.FALGUNI D.TRIVEDI(3912) for the Defendant(s) No. 3 NOTICE SERVED for the Defendant(s) No. 2 ==========================================================
 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE SANDEEP N. BHATT  Date : 15/07/2024

sentences.text: ORAL ORDER 1.

The present appeal is filed by the appellant - Insurance Company under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and award dated 6.8.2019 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Auxi) at Mahuva in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.77 of 2017, by which, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition by awarding Rs.2,39,265/- with 9% p.a. interest to be paid to claimant/s, by holding opponents liable, jointly and severally.

sentences.text:
2. The facts of the present appeal are as under :
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/5382/2019 ORDER DATED: 15/07/2024 undefined 2.1

The claimant filed the claim petition claiming compensation by stating that on The United India Insurance Co Ltd vs Bharatbhai Ganeshbhai Baraiya on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121479568/
1 15.7.2007, at about 9.30 p.m., the claimant was going on the Motorcycle No.GJ.4AL.7647 and when he reached near Saibaba Ginning Mill at Veravadar road,
at that time, the opponent no.1 came by driving his Motorcycle No.GJ.4AK.1002 in full speed and on wrong side of the road and dashed with the Motorcycle with the Motorcycle of the claimant, due to which the claimant sustained serious injuries.

sentences.text:
The FIR was lodged against the opponent no.1.
2.2
The notices were served to the opponents.
Opponents filed their written statements.
The issues were framed by the Tribunal.
Oral as well as documentary evidence were led before the Tribunal.
After hearing the submissions made by the rival parties, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition(s) and awarded compensation as noted above.
2.3 Hence, the insurance company has filed the present appeal before this Court.

3. Learned advocate for the appellant - Insurance Company has submitted that the claimant was going on his motorcycle and he dashed head on with another motorcycle insured by the appellant and therefore the negligent of the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/5382/2019 ORDER DATED: 15/07/2024 undefined claimant ought to have been at 50%.
Further, as there was no proof of income and the accident of the year 2007, the income should have been considered only as per minimum wages and the interest rate should have much less than 9%.
He, therefore, prayed that all these counts, this appeal is required to be allowed and the award is required to be modified accordingly.

4. Per Contra, learned advocates for the original claimant and the original owner of the vehicle insured with the appellant-insurance company have submitted that the impugned judgment and award is just and proper and the point of negligence and quantum are held by the learned Tribunal,
after considering the evidence led before it and the settled proposition of law.

They, therefore,
prayed to dismiss this appeal.
5. I have considered the submissions made by the respective parties.
I have perused the record and proceedings.
I have gone through the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.
I have also considered the pleadings of the parties before the Tribunal.

The learned Tribunal has discussed the point of negligence and observed that there is nothing contrary coming in the cross-examination of the claimant to negate his say in the complaint that the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/5382/2019 ORDER DATED: 15/07/2024 undefined claimant

was going on his motorcycle and when he reached near Saibaba Ginning Mill at Velavadar road, the opponent no.1 came by driving his motorcycle in full speed and wrong side of the road and dashed with his motorcycle.

Further, from the documentary evidence i.e. FIR, panchanama, injury certificate and disability certificate prove that the vehicle of the opponent no.1 was involved in the accident, due to which the claimant received injuries.

Further, the opponent no.1 has not stepped into the witness box to explain as to how the accident had occurred and therefore the learned Tribunal has held that adverse inference can be drawn against the driver of the offending vehicle and there is no reason to disbelieve the say of the The United India Insurance Co Ltd vs Bharatbhai Ganeshbhai Baraiya on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121479568/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 2 claimant.
There is no reason to interfere with the said observation made by the learned Tribunal.

6. On the point of quantum, the learned Tribunal has assessed the monthly income on the basis of the minimum wages as mentioned in the discussion and calculated the amount of compensation by considering the permanent partial disability occurred by the claimant, applying the multiplier as applicable, the medical expenditure and other expenses incurred by the claimant due to the accident and awarded the amount of compensation, which is just and proper.

It is noteworthy to mention that the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 which gives NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/5382/2019 ORDER DATED: 15/07/2024 undefined paramount importance to the concept of `just and fair' compensation.
It is a beneficial legislation which has been framed with the object of providing relief to the victims or their families.

Section 168 of the Motor Vehicles Act deals with the concept of `just compensation' which ought to be determined on the foundation of fairness,
reasonableness and equitability.

Although such determination can never be arithmetically exact or perfect, an endeavour should be made by the Court to award just and fair compensation irrespective of the amount claimed by the claimants.
Considering this principle, the amount awarded cannot be considered to be on the higher side.
7. There are catena of decisions that the award of the rate of interest is the discretion of the Tribunal which should be exercised by considering the facts and circumstances of each case.

The provisions of MV Act are benevolent legislation and normally it should be construed that the provisions of the MV Act are enacted to see that the claimants could get some amount of compensation where the claimants either lose their bread earner or has received serious injuries.
There cannot be any perfect arithmetic calculation for awarding amount of calculation.

Therefore, the appeal is required to be dismissed as the learned Tribunal has considered all the aspects and awarded the compensation NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/5382/2019 ORDER DATED: 15/07/2024 undefined to the claimant,
which is not required to be interfered with in this appeal.
This appeal is, therefore, required to be dismissed.
8. In view of above ,the following order is passed.
8.1 The present appeal is dismissed with no order as to costs.

8.2 The amount lying with the Tribunal and/or in the FDR, pursuant to the order of this Court if any, shall be disbursed to the claimant, along with accrued interest thereon if any, by account payee cheque, after proper verification and after following due procedure, within a period of six weeks from today.
8.3 Record and proceedings be sent back to the concerned Tribunal, forthwith.
(SANDEEP N. BHATT,J) SRILATHA
